html:
Dvaravati was a Buddhist culture of the Mon people in central Thailand, from about the 600s to the 1000s. Chinese pilgrims of the mid 600s called it To-lo-po-ti and placed it between the Khmer lands to the east and the Pyu to the west. Silver coins found there bear the Sanskrit words "merit of the lord of Dvaravati".

It may have been one kingdom or a loose group of moated towns, such as Nakhon Pathom, U Thong and Lopburi. Its people were early followers of Theravada Buddhism, and they left stone wheels of the law and fine Buddha images.

From the 900s the Khmer Empire took over Lopburi and much of the region. A Mon kingdom, Haripunchai, lasted in the north until 1292. Thai states such as Sukhothai and Ayutthaya later inherited the Buddhism and art of Dvaravati.
